purpose: Lightweight map for distributing Confluence of Minds content inside existing communities without turning the project into a cross-posting machine. This map guides discovery and contribution style; it is not a publishing schedule.
principles: Distribute the question, idea or useful observation before the work itself.
Prefer joining an existing relevant conversation over creating a promotional thread.
Only mention a CoM world or Confluence when it genuinely adds context or value.
Never mass-post the same comment or link across multiple communities.
Before contributing, check the current community rules, self-promotion policy and thread context.
No automated external posting unless the platform is explicitly connected and the community rules permit it.
If the contribution would read like advertising without the CoM link, do not publish it.
Prefer one strong community opportunity over ten weak ones.

default_workflow.discover: Find a current discussion, question or request for recommendations that strongly overlaps a CoM theme.
default_workflow.qualify: Check recency, relevance, community rules, contribution value and self-promotion risk.
default_workflow.contribute: Write a native reply that answers the discussion first. Mention/link CoM only if it materially enriches the answer.
default_workflow.limit: Default to at most one external-community contribution per editorial cycle unless two clearly independent, high-value opportunities exist.

reddit.best_use: Existing threads where people are already discussing the exact scientific, cultural, creative or narrative question touched by a CoM world.
reddit.publication_style: Answer-first, link-second. Avoid standalone self-promotional submissions by default.
reddit.automation_level_now: Discovery, scoring and drafting can be automated. Posting still requires a Reddit-capable connection or manual posting.
reddit.notes: Use a dedicated human-looking CoM/Thomas account, not a disposable bot identity. Build normal participation history rather than appearing only when promoting a link.

specialist_forums_and_communities.best_use: Niche communities for interactive fiction, audio drama, speculative biology, worldbuilding, historical Japan or AI creativity.
specialist_forums_and_communities.publication_style: Native contribution or project share only when community norms explicitly support it.
specialist_forums_and_communities.automation_level_now: Discovery and drafting only unless a legitimate write integration is available.

conversation_hooks: Could humans fly on Titan?
Why explore Titan rather than another moon?
What makes Titan scientifically strange?
How much realism should a science-fiction game preserve?
What would actually fail first in a Titan mission?
worlds.contribution_rule: Lead with the science or design answer. Mention Incident on Titan only after providing useful context.

conversation_hooks: What did Shogun simplify or make people curious about?
Who was the historical Anjin?
Which details of Edo-period culture are most misunderstood?
When does historical adaptation become its own fiction?
worlds.contribution_rule: Answer the historical/cultural question first. Avoid presenting CoM as an authority on Japan.

conversation_hooks: Why are crossroads cities so powerful in fantasy?
How can Silk Road history inspire worldbuilding without copying it?
What makes a fictional city feel culturally layered?
worlds.contribution_rule: Provide the worldbuilding/history insight first; mention Chronicles of Kashgar only as an example of applying the idea.

conversation_hooks: Could any dragon trait be biologically plausible?
Why do dragon myths recur across cultures?
How would engineered dragons actually work?
What makes creature design feel internally coherent?
worlds.contribution_rule: Make the biological/worldbuilding thought interesting on its own before mentioning Shattered Dragons.

conversation_hooks: Can climate fiction remain adventurous rather than didactic?
What happens when a novel behaves like a game?
How can environmental stakes become mechanics rather than exposition?
worlds.contribution_rule: Discuss narrative form and climate storytelling first; mention the book only when it directly answers the thread.

conversation_hooks: What does authorship mean with generative AI?
Can readers identify AI-written fiction?
What changes when the reader becomes the commissioner or editor?
Were people imagining machine-written books before ChatGPT?
worlds.contribution_rule: Engage the authorship/publishing question substantively; use Authentiques Victimes as a historical/creative example, not as the thesis.

conversation_hooks: Can AI-generated work be judged like human performance?
What makes an AI creation surprising rather than merely competent?
Should creative AI competitions judge prompts, outputs or systems?
worlds.contribution_rule: Start from the judging/creativity problem; mention AI's Got Talent as an experiment around that question.

conversation_hooks: Can a film exist without images?
What makes binaural fiction genuinely immersive?
Why does removing images sometimes increase visual imagination?
Where does audio drama end and cinema begin?
worlds.contribution_rule: Talk craft and listening experience first; link SILMEA only when someone is explicitly interested in comparable work.

conversation_hooks: Why can fairy tales survive endless retellings?
When does a retelling become a genuinely new story?
Can ecological themes enter a fairy tale without becoming a lecture?
worlds.contribution_rule: Discuss the retelling question first; mention Queen of Ashes as one interpretation only when relevant.

conversation_hooks: Why do societies solve technically harder problems but fail on obvious collective ones?
What makes climate communication provoke action rather than agreement?
Is inaction a knowledge problem or a coordination problem?
worlds.contribution_rule: Contribute analysis rather than moralizing. Do not revive old statistics without current verification.
